excerpts: # Rewriting TTS Inference Economics: Lightning V2 on Tenstorrent Achieves 4× Lower Cost Than NVIDIA L40S
AI voice agent connecting legal client calls with intake, qualification, and appointment scheduling workflows.
The world’s first TTS model to deliver high-quality speech synthesis under joint BlockFloat8 quantization and reduced-precision arithmetic.
### Key Highlights
* _4× lower on-prem inference cost vs NVIDIA L40S_
* _~3.6× higher effective compute throughput at the same system cost, enabling ~4× higher concurrency_
* _95%+ of layers running in LoFi computational fidelity without measurable audio degradation_
* _80%+ of the model deployed in BlockFloat8 (BFP8)_
* _~2× model size reduction via BFP8_
* _Zero audible artifacts despite aggressive numerical optimization_
* _Lightning V2 is the world’s first TTS model to combine computational fidelity and BlockFloat8 at production audio quality_
## Why Text-to-Speech Is More Numerically Fragile Than LLMs or Image Models

Text-to-Speech is fundamentally more numerically fragile than LLMs because it generates a **continuous waveform** , not discrete tokens. In language models, small quantization errors perturb probability distributions — the next token might change, yet the output often remains coherent due to natural reset points at token boundaries. In TTS, however, every numerical value directly contributes to audible signal energy. There is no boundary to absorb error. A small perturbation does not merely shift probabilities — it alters phase, harmonic structure, and waveform continuity. What is statistically minor in an LLM can become perceptually obvious in audio.

Speech also spans a wide dynamic range within milliseconds — from low-energy fricatives to high-energy vowels and rapid transients. When precision is reduced (e.g., with BlockFloat8 or LoFi compute), small numerical deviations can collapse low-energy phonemes, introduce background hiss, distort timbre, or cause pitch instability. Quantization error is not averaged out; it manifests as structured acoustic artifacts. In speech models, error affects perception — and the human auditory system is far less forgiving.

excerpts: ## Real-Time Voice AI Architecture: STT + LLM + TTS + Telephony
Real-Time Voice AI Architecture: STT + LLM + TTS + Telephony
Real-time voice AI architecture, explained: STT, LLM, TTS, and telephony, plus latency budgets, streaming pipelines, and production design tradeoffs.

Voice AI architecture is the wiring diagram for a system that can listen, understand, speak back, and do it fast enough to pass as a normal conversation. Speech recognition, language reasoning, speech synthesis, and telephony each do a specific kind of translation, but the handoffs between them decide whether the experience feels snappy or painfully delayed.

Humans have a tight tolerance for dead air. A system has to hear a user, interpret intent, decide what to say, and start talking back inside a window that feels conversational. Miss that window and users talk over it, repeat themselves, or abandon the interaction. Land it and the technology fades into the background.
## The Four Pillars of Voice AI Architecture

Real-time voice systems tend to converge on the same four-layer stack. You can swap vendors and models, but you cannot wish away the layers: each one comes with its own latency budget, its own ways to fail, and its own knobs to tune. If you want to debug why a voice agent feels “slow” or “off,” you start by understanding what each layer is responsible for.
_Each layer of the voice AI stack handles a distinct transformation of data._

citations.title: Smallest AI names ex-CRED, YES Bank, Kotak digital banking leader Siddharth Sharma President – BFSI, India
excerpts: # Smallest AI names ex-CRED, YES Bank, Kotak digital banking leader Siddharth Sharma President – BFSI, India
ANI | Updated: Nov 06, 2026 15:49 IST
[ani-trusted-source](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=aninews.in)
[ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Va7q7004dTnMVl9H9r0o)

Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], November 6 (ANI): [Smallest AI](https://smallest.ai/) , a San Francisco-based foundational AI research lab, has appointed Siddharth Sharma as President of Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance, India. In his role, Sharma will own revenue and partnerships for the company's growing BFSI business, working directly with co-founder and CEO Sudarshan Kamath.

The appointment follows the company's [$21 million](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/smallestai-gets-21-million-in-funding-to-build-voice-4-0--the-next-generation-of-enterprise-voice-ai-302839266.html) funding round announced in July 2026 and the growing demand from Indian banks, NBFCs, and insurers for voice AI solutions that can handle collections and customer-service calls in the languages their customers actually speak. Smallest AI builds its own speech recognition and synthesis models, covers over 14+ Indian languages alongside English, and supports self-hosted deployment inside a customer's own infrastructure — a requirement for most regulated institutions.

"BFSI is now one of our strongest verticals in India, and requires localized leadership to continue providing the level of support our customers expect," said Sudarshan Kamath, co-founder and CEO, Smallest AI. “Banks expect a partner who understands how they evaluate, govern and scale technology. Siddharth has built digital banking businesses inside India's largest banks, and has a history of building mutually-beneficial financial partnerships. We’re looking forward to his leadership in this sector as Smallest AI grows.”

Sharma has spent over 20 years in banking and financial services, across ICICI, YES Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and CRED. During his time at CRED, he led partnerships with banks and financial institutions. At Kotak Mahindra Bank, he was Vice President and Head of Go-to-Market for Digital Initiatives. Before that, Sharma was Senior Vice President at YES Bank, where he worked across Unified Payments Interface (UPI), wallets, Bharat Bill Payment System (BBPS), and the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS). He was most recently Vice President, Credit & Strategy, at CashFlo.

"Indian banks need voice AI that works in the customer's language, on a real phone line, at the scale of a national loan book; all without sensitive data leaving their control," said Siddharth Sharma, President – BFSI, India, Smallest AI. “Collections and service calls are the areas where that need is sharpest. Very few companies build the underlying speech models and can run them inside a bank's own infrastructure. I believe that Smallest AI has the combination to solve this issue and am excited to work alongside Sudarshan and his team to support these customers.”

Based in Mumbai, Sharma will lead Smallest AI's go-to-market with banks, NBFCs, insurers, and financial-services partners. He’ll be responsible for building the Smallest AI partner network in the sector, and shaping how its voice agents are deployed across collections, servicing and onboarding.
About Smallest AI

Smallest AI is a foundational AI research lab building the next generation of real-time voice AI infrastructure for enterprises. The company develops speech recognition, speech generation, and speech-to-speech systems designed to enable natural, scalable AI conversations across customer service, healthcare, financial services, and other high-volume communication environments. Headquartered in San Francisco, Smallest AI serves enterprises globally through its Voice 4.0 platform and proprietary AI models, including Lightning TTS and Pulse STT. The company is backed by Seligman Ventures, Sierra Ventures, 3one4 Capital, Better Capital, Upsparks Capital, Schema Ventures, Tiny VC, DeVC, Mission Street Capital, and other angel investors. (ANI)

## How Smallest AI works
Smallest AI is voice infrastructure. Two product lines share one account, one API key, and one set of docs.

* **Voice Agents** is the hosted platform for agents that talk to your customers over the phone, on the web, or inside a mobile app. It runs speech to text, the LLM turn, text to speech, and telephony for you. Configure an agent in the dashboard, or write the LLM turn yourself with the Agent Crew SDK.

* **Models** are the individual engines behind it: Lightning (text to speech), Pulse (speech to text), Hydra (speech to speech), and Electron (LLM). Call them over HTTP or WebSocket from any stack, including Pipecat, LiveKit, and the Vercel AI SDK.

AI voice agent connecting legal client calls with intake, qualification, and appointment scheduling workflows.
Explore Smallest.ai's Lightning V3, a breakthrough text-to-speech model for highly natural and responsive voice agents. Read the full announcement.

_Lightning V3.1 is our most natural-sounding TTS model to date, based on neutral third-party and customer evaluation. It supports 15 languages: English, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Swedish, Portuguese, German, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi, and Gujarati, with automatic language detection and mid-sentence language switching.

Lightning V3.2 extends the V3 architecture with instruction-following capability. The model accepts explicit directives for emotional register, pitch variation, and volume control, including low-energy output states like whispering that are difficult to achieve through prosody modeling alone._
